title: Case: Shipper of a glass lampshade sent abroad writes about the replies to his damage claim
context: Cosmo Eckersall sent a hand-painted glass lampshade to a buyer abroad on DL-4149 with Oxenhale Arc's added cover. It was delivered on 22 February and he has claimed for damage under reference CL-9895.
initial_request: Please somebody explain me. First letter say too late, 21 days. I explain: lady who buy the lamp shade she not speak my language, I not speak hers, we write with translator in telephone, photos take long time. And I telephone you 29 February to say is broken, this you have. Then second letter say not too late, but no photo of box. Now third again too late and nobody look anymore. Which one is true? You change reason every time I answer. Lady maybe still have box, I can ask her. But I not go ask her again for nothing if you say after again too late. I pay for insurance on this parcel. Glass is in pieces. DL-4149.

CL-9895 reviewed. Call log shows damage first reported 3 Mar, day 7, so the claim was made in time. Declined on evidence: three photos of the item, none of the outer packaging. We cannot assess packing or transit damage without one. Claim decisions and appeals on damage sit with this team.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Oxenhale Arc Logistics
events.body: CL-9895: our record still shows closed, out of time. The 21 days run from delivery to receipt of the completed claim form, not to a phone call. We administer claim intake and the file is shut on our system, so no further evidence will be looked at. Please do not ask the shipper for more.

acceptable_actions.summary: Set out the two contradictory positions on CL-9895 and ask which stands and whether a packaging photo would now be considered.

must: Sends the contradiction on CL-9895 to Delivery investigations by Email and asks them to settle which position stands

States both positions with their source: Delivery investigations on 24 March (in time from the 29 February call, declined for no packaging photo) and Parcel trace team on 27 March (out of time, file shut, no further evidence)
Asks whether a photo of the outer packaging from the buyer would be considered if supplied now, before the shipper is asked to get one
Tells the team the shipper has been refused three times on two different grounds, and that evidence has to come from a buyer abroad who shares no language with him, so each request costs him time
must_not: Tells the shipper the claim is out of time, or that it was made in time, as a settled fact
Promises or implies that the cover will pay, or that the claim will be reopened or accepted
Tells the shipper to get a packaging photo from the buyer as though it will reopen the claim, before the owning team has said it would be considered
Replies to the shipper with only the time limit or a statement that the file is closed
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: CL-9895 / DL-4149 (glass lampshade, delivered abroad 22 February, shipper Cosmo Eckersall, cover purchased). The desk holds two written positions that cannot both be right. Yours of 24 March: damage first reported by phone 29 February, day 7, so the claim was made in time; declined because there is no photo of the outer packaging. Parcel trace team, 27 March: closed as out of time because the form arrived on day 24, file shut, no further evidence will be looked at. The shipper has now been refused three times on two different grounds. He says the buyer may still have the box and he can ask her for a photo, but she is abroad, they share no language and work through a translation app, so he does not want to ask again unless it will count. Please confirm in writing which position stands, and whether a packaging photo supplied now would be assessed. I have told him neither outcome and promised nothing.
